Husband = 401(k) 400,000 pre-tax at 24% marginal (library/tax_rates_assumed.md stated assumption; at 12% his side is 710,000/gap 96,992; at 32% his side is 630,000/gap 16,992) = 304,000; brokerage 300,000 minus 15% on embedded gain 80,000 (12,000; add 3,040 if NIIT is applied to investment gains - the library states NIIT on the house gain only, so that extension is [unverified]) = 288,000; cash 50,000 + Tacoma 20,000 = 662,000. Nominal 'equal halves' leave wife 613,008/662,000 = 92.6% of husband, a gap of 48,992. Excludes the undisclosed bonus (below), which is itself marital property; client confirms bonuses recur (prior year ~40,000, her report).

maintenance_tax_treatment: The proposal's 'deductible to Husband and taxable to Wife' is legally wrong for any decree executed after Dec 31, 2018: alimony is neither deductible by the payor nor includible by the recipient (TCJA §11051 per library/irc_1041_121_71.md). The decree must not repeat that language. Practical effect: Husband's $2,000/month costs him un-deducted dollars (more than he thinks), and Wife receives it tax-free; child support is never deductible or includible. Note Columbia still adds maintenance to the recipient's and subtracts it from the payor's income when computing child support (library/columbia_child_support_guidelines.md). Consider structuring maintenance as direct payment of the mortgage/housing costs in the A2 scenario.
dependents_and_filing_status: Wife has the children ~70% of the time, so she is the custodial parent and may claim both children by default under §152(e); Husband's 'alternating years' plan requires Wife to sign Form 8332, which moves only the child tax credit - head-of-household status, EITC and the dependent-care credit stay with Wife regardless (§§2(b), 152(e); Form 8332; library/filing_status_dependents.md). Do not agree to the alternating-claim term without charging for it (the credit's dollar amount is not in the library - flag). Wife should qualify for head of household (children with her >half the year; she must pay >half the cost of the home - confirm). Marital status is fixed on Dec 31 (§7703(a)): if the decree is final on or before 12/31/2026 she files single/HoH and no joint return is available that year - which drives the timing of any house sale to capture the $500,000 §121 joint exclusion (Scenario B only; A2 does not need the joint return).
